purpose: First real batch committed through the pages contract built in PR #43. Until now every `search` event in the store came from the separate search_metrics.py call that contract replaced.

why_the_agent_cannot_time_its_own_search.bracketing_two_shell_timestamps_measures: the whole turn, not the call
why_the_agent_cannot_time_its_own_search.bracket_includes: model token generation for both surrounding tool calls
why_the_agent_cannot_time_its_own_search.conclusion: A required duration_ms on this path can only be satisfied by inventing a number or by reporting the task skipped and discarding real candidates.

wave.browser_route: not exercised; browseros-neo was not reachable this session

web_search_tasks.note: 9 results: 7 aggregator listing pages, 2 individual postings. One is remote-labelled and skipped per the 2026-09-23 remote removal; the other sits on a recruitment-agency host absent from the source catalog, so it cannot carry a known source_id into an envelope.
9 results, all aggregator listing pages, no individual posting.

recorded_events.note: `round` is missing because this was a discovery wave, not a full user-facing round; `search` is observed, which is the thing this contract exists to guarantee.

store_wide_effect.note: The 3 events carrying a latency are pre-#43 and came from search_metrics.py. Without reported_rate the p50 of 1800ms would have represented 3 of 5 pages with nothing saying so.

limitations: Nothing distinguishes an executor that cannot measure from one that did not bother; the declaration is recorded, not proved.
The web_search channel committed zero candidates this run. The open web returns mostly aggregator listing pages, and an individual posting still needs a host that is in the source catalog.
The browser channel was not exercised and remains unverified in a real round.
Timing for a browser-executed search is unaffected: that executor has a clock and still reports `measured`.
